### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via TranslationConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const), defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via defaultLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), fallbackLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), sourceLocale (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), supportedLocales (literal, a string literal in TranslationConfigSchema), os i18n check (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts), os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via os i18n extract (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os lint (command, 46 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `abb1da85aa3a69bec3ee8ca3fa861688e289ccb7` — the merge of head `bbf55f564550b67ba7a1fe46013afe6db77148e3` into base `e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin abb1da85aa3a69bec3ee8ca3fa861688e289ccb7 && git checkout abb1da85aa3a69bec3ee8ca3fa861688e289ccb7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469 bbf55f564550b67ba7a1fe46013afe6db77148e3 && git checkout -B drift-repro e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469 && git merge --no-ff bbf55f564550b67ba7a1fe46013afe6db77148e3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e9884e199ec237004dc210d7c8b08e3615b5b469` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `34ec0e4f9c46dec9537c4a5525870753f7d4b24d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-bundle-extract.ts

Read for this record: card #33232 (body, triage 6874060759, claim 6878868326, relayed os-dev-report 6881427009), PR #33357 (body, 14-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read on `origin/main` only to judge the scope files. No ruling and no earlier contract-review record exists on the card or the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`TranslationConfigSchema` accept set: widened, right.** `sourceLocale` is a new optional `LocaleSchema` key on a `strictObject`. Before this head, `i18n: { sourceLocale: ... }` was refused as an unknown key, so every stack that parses on `main` parses to the same output here. No existing valid stack changes meaning.
- **Three near-miss keys (`sourceLanguage`, `authoringLocale`, `authoringLanguage`): still refused, right.** They were refused before with the generic unknown-key answer and are refused now with `sourceLocale` as the suggestion. The accept set does not move; only the message does.
- **Public type surface: widened, right.** `TranslationConfig` (a `z.input`) gains one optional property. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` gains exactly `system/TranslationConfig:sourceLocale`, and the regenerated reference row matches the `.describe()` string word for word.
- **`@objectstack/cli` exported surface: unchanged, right.** `resolveSourceLocale` is exported from `utils/i18n-coverage.ts`, which the package's `exports` map (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `./package.json`) does not address.
- **CLI behaviour for stacks without the key: unchanged, right.** `resolveSourceLocale` returns `defaultLocale`, else `en`, which is the expression it replaces in both `computeI18nCoverage` and `extract.ts`. The flag still precedes it at all three call sites.
- **Gated locale set when the key IS declared: narrowed in one shape, wrong as documented.** See ④ finding 1.
- **Gate verdicts:** every check-run on the head concluded success or skipped. That includes Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Test Core 1 to 8, and both type-check families. No check failed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — correct. The PR body and the changeset both carry the line, and the diff widens a published schema's accept set and its exported input type.

`@objectstack/spec: minor` and `@objectstack/cli: minor` match what the diff publishes: one new optional authorable key, and a new CLI reading that only a stack declaring the key can reach. Nothing is removed or narrowed for existing input, so major is not owed. A patch would understate a new authorable key. Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation, refused GitHub writes:** process only. The seat opened the draft PR from the pushed branch and relayed the report verbatim; the tree reviewed here is the pushed head.
- **Dev deviation, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` surface breach:** accepted. The old row ("Defaults to the config's `i18n.defaultLocale`") is false against `resolveSourceLocale`; the new row states the order the code implements.
- **Dev deviation, gate rerun narrowed to 56 commands for the last commit:** moot. The check-runs on this head are the gate verdicts and all are green.
- **Dev deviation, Clause-② measured on the built declarations:** agrees with ① and ②.
- **Open question 1 (should the serving layer read `sourceLocale`): answered A, and escalated.** The schema jsdoc, the docs page and the changeset all publish "not yet read by the serving layer". That is true on `main`: `metaTranslateOptions` passes `getDefaultLocale()` as `ResolveOptions.defaultLocale`, and `serve.ts` collapses the fallback to `fallbackLocale`, else `defaultLocale`. The follow-up card the PR body promises is not filed: an issue search for `sourceLocale` returns only #33232. It is owed before this lands, because until it exists "not yet" points at nothing. It also carries a consequence the PR creates: with the key declared and no `fallbackLocale`, the gate reports the source locale 100% covered while an `en` request is served the `zh-CN` row.
- **Open question 2 (`os i18n check --json` keeps `defaultLocale` for the resolved source locale): answered A.** The `CoverageReport` doc comment states it and the output is unchanged for stacks without the key.
- **Out-of-scope finding, skills docs:** `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` follow-up is declared on the `Skills-docs:` line but not filed. It is owed to the skills lane.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is owed. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — judged against card #33232 (no ruling, no ADR cited) and its first consumer, `computeI18nCoverage`.

The design holds for the card's scenario. One key carried two facts; the new key separates them, defaults to today's reading, uses the same `LocaleSchema`, and carries no `supportedLocales` membership rule, as `defaultLocale` carries none. In the downstream shape (`defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, `sourceLocale: 'en'`, `zh-CN` in `supportedLocales`) the consumer gives zero `en` findings and reports the `zh-CN` gap. The serving-layer caveat is stated in the jsdoc and is true.

1. **should-fix — the jsdoc sentence "they do gate every other declared locale, `defaultLocale` included" is false for a shape the same jsdoc permits.**
   - In `computeI18nCoverage` the gated set is the source locale, plus `supportedLocales`, plus the locales some bundle exists for. The users' `defaultLocale` is never added.
   - On `main` it was always in the set, because it was the source.
   - So `{ defaultLocale: 'zh-CN', sourceLocale: 'en', supportedLocales: ['en', 'es-ES'] }` with no `zh-CN` bundle yet, or the same with `supportedLocales: []`, gates `en` and `es-ES` and reports nothing for `zh-CN`. That is the language every user without a preference is served, and the card's own failure ("loses its zh-CN coverage check") in a narrower shape.
   - `extract.ts` has the same root: `zh-CN` is no longer scaffolded there, though its `--locales` help still says the default locale is always included.
   - Fix either side: add the declared `defaultLocale` to the active set in the three non-override arms (and to the extract locale list), with a test for the shape; or narrow the sentence to "every locale in `supportedLocales`". The first is what the card asks for.

2. **nit — the `.describe()` string omits the serving caveat the jsdoc carries.** The generated reference row and any schema-driven tooltip show only the `.describe()` text, so a reader there is not told the runtime does not read the key. Fixing it regenerates the reference and moves the head; take it with finding 1's fix or leave it to the open-question-1 card.

**Implementing files**

- `i18n-coverage.ts`: `resolveSourceLocale` agrees with the contract sentence by sentence (`sourceLocale`, else `defaultLocale`, else `en`; empty strings skipped; non-object input tolerated). The override precedes it. The `CoverageReport.defaultLocale` and `CoverageOptions.defaultLocale` comments describe what the code does. Finding 1 lives in the unchanged `activeLocales` block below it.
- `extract.ts`: the same single reading, flag first; the comment matches. Finding 1's extract half applies.
- `i18n-bundle-extract.ts`: comment only, and accurate. The source locale is rewritten from the inline text on every merge, as the changeset says.
- `check.ts`, `lint.ts`: the three `--default-locale` help strings state the implemented order.
- **nit** — unchanged neighbours in `check.ts` and `lint.ts` still say "non-default locales" where the code now means non-source: the `--strict` help at `check.ts:114`, the `--i18n-strict` help at `lint.ts:937`, and the closing message at `check.ts:261`. With the key declared, strict mode does raise the users' default locale to an error, which those words exclude. Follow-up or accepted deviation.

Break attempts that held:
- Key absent: the report is identical to the pre-change reading.
- Key equal to `defaultLocale`: identical.
- Key outside `supportedLocales`: the source is added to the gated set and satisfied by inline text.
- `--default-locale` set: it wins.
- Stack composition: `i18n` is a `single` key in `COMPOSE_KEY_DISPOSITIONS`, so the new key is not dropped or merged.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5nhu4dRbKVQKDB4CDB`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `18a92291f457c77cb4f93f4ee32001f3c78e93d2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/extract.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/i18n/check.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-bundle-extract.ts

Delta review of the hop `34ec0e4f9c46` to `18a92291f457`, against record 6882834204 on the earlier head. Read for this record: that record, every PR comment after it (only this seat's claim line; no dev report and no ruling record was posted on the PR or on card #33232 after it), the two PR commits of the hop (`c703b3bdd`, `18a92291f`), the head versions of the scope files, the check-runs on the head, and issues #33634 and #33635. The hop holds no merge of `main`, so the whole compare is the PR's own change. It adds no implementing file, so the `Scope:` line is unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`TranslationConfigSchema` accept set: unchanged in the hop, right.** The hop edits the `sourceLocale` jsdoc and its `.describe()` string only. No key, type or refinement moves.
- **Public type surface: unchanged in the hop, right.** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` is not touched, and the regenerated reference row in `content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx` matches the new `.describe()` string word for word.
- **`@objectstack/cli` exported surface: unchanged, right.** `withGatedDefaultLocale` is a new export of `utils/i18n-coverage.ts`, which the package's `exports` map does not address.
- **Gated locale set, key declared: widened to include the users' `defaultLocale`, right.** The three config-reading arms of `computeI18nCoverage` now append it; the `--locales` arm does not. This closes finding 1 of the earlier record.
- **Gated locale set, key absent: unchanged, right.** `resolveGatedDefaultLocale` returns `undefined` unless `sourceLocale` is a non-empty string, and `withGatedDefaultLocale` then returns the same array. A test deep-equals the report against the pre-change reading.
- **`os i18n extract` locale list: widened the same way, right.** `extractTranslations` reads a missing list as the source locale alone and always puts the source first, so appending `defaultLocale` adds one scaffolded locale and drops none.
- **Gate verdicts:** all 68 check-runs on the head concluded success (58) or skipped (10). That includes Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Build Docs, Test Core 1 to 8, and every type-check family. No check failed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes — still correct, and the level is unchanged. `@objectstack/spec: minor` and `@objectstack/cli: minor` match what the PR publishes. The hop adds no key and removes nothing. Its one behaviour change, more locales gated and scaffolded, is reachable only by a stack that declares the new key, so it sits inside the same minor. The changeset states it. Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Serving-layer follow-up (earlier ③, open question 1): filed, closed.** #33634 is open, labelled `domain:server`, cites record 6882834204, and carries the consequence that record named: with the key declared and no `fallbackLocale`, the gate reports the source locale covered while an `en` request is served the `zh-CN` row. The PR body points at it. "Not yet read by the serving layer" now points at a card.
- **Skills-docs follow-up (earlier ③): filed, closed.** #33635 is open, labelled `domain:skills`, blocked by #33232, and names the `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` rows to add. The PR body's `Skills-docs:` line names it.
- **Changeset `Skills-docs:` line still reads "follow-up owed" with no number.** The PR body carries #33635; the changeset does not. This is the prose face and belongs to the lane seat's ACCEPT, not to this record. Check Changeset is green.
- **Behaviour the hop publishes, monolingual arm:** a stack declaring `sourceLocale` with `supportedLocales: []` and no bundle used to report nothing and now reports every key missing in `defaultLocale`. This is the fix the earlier record asked for, it is tested, and the changeset and docs page state it.
- **Earlier flags that do not move:** the `cli.mdx` surface breach stays accepted (the hop edits one more row there, for the strict-mode wording, and the row is true); open question 2 stays answered A.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is owed. The PR is still a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**Findings of the earlier record**

1. **should-fix, jsdoc claim that `defaultLocale` is gated: closed, by the code route.**
   - `computeI18nCoverage` passes the three non-override arms through `withGatedDefaultLocale`, so a declared `defaultLocale` is gated beside a declared `sourceLocale` whatever `supportedLocales` and the bundles hold.
   - `extract.ts` passes its default list through the same function, so `zh-CN` is scaffolded; its `--locales` help now says so.
   - The jsdoc is rewritten to "they gate every locale in `supportedLocales` plus `defaultLocale`, even when `supportedLocales` omits it", which is what the code does.
   - Tests cover the exact shape the earlier record gave (`supportedLocales: ['en', 'es-ES']`, no `zh-CN` bundle), both `supportedLocales: []` arms, the `--locales` exception, the key-absent identity, and the extract scaffold.
2. **nit, `.describe()` omitted the serving caveat: closed.** The string now ends with the caveat, and the generated reference row carries it.
3. **nit, "non-default locales" wording in `check.ts` and `lint.ts`: closed.** The `--strict` help, the `--i18n-strict` help, the closing hint of `os i18n check`, and the `cli.mdx` row now say non-source.

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — the hop's change holds against its first consumer. Each sentence of the new jsdoc and `.describe()` was read against `computeI18nCoverage`, `extract.ts` and the serving code on `main`, and each is true.

**Implementing files**

- `i18n-coverage.ts`: `resolveGatedDefaultLocale` and `withGatedDefaultLocale` agree with their comments and with the schema jsdoc. The rule is one function shared by the gate and the scaffold, so the two cannot drift.
- `extract.ts`: agrees. The source-hash loop reads the widened list, so a `zh-CN` hash table is picked up as well.
- `check.ts`, `lint.ts`: wording only, and accurate.
- `i18n-bundle-extract.ts`: not touched in the hop.

**New findings in the hop: nits only**

- **nit** — the schema jsdoc states the gated set without the `--locales` exception. The changeset, the code comment and the tests carry it. Accepted deviation.
- **nit** — the `--locales` help of `os i18n check` still reads "default: the config's i18n.supportedLocales, else every locale found" and does not name the added `defaultLocale`, where extract's help does. The `--fill` help of `os i18n extract` and one comment beside it still say "non-default locales". Follow-up or accepted deviation.
- **nit** — with a `--default-locale` override on a stack that declares `sourceLocale`, the declared `defaultLocale` is gated even when `sourceLocale` equals it; a stack without the key and the same override does not gate it. The override case is one run, and gating the users' default there is the safer reading. Accepted deviation.

Break attempts that held:
- Key absent: the same array is returned, and the report is identical.
- Key equal to `defaultLocale`, no override: the source is already first in the set, nothing is appended; in extract the set dedupes it.
- `supportedLocales: []` with existing bundles: `zh-CN` is appended to the discovered set, and no discovered locale is dropped.
- Extract with no declared list: the list becomes `defaultLocale` alone and `extractTranslations` prepends the source, so both are emitted.
- Explicit `--locales`: untouched in both commands.

## 维护者速读 · PR #33357 @ `bbf55f56` · 2026-11-15T05:53Z

- 改了什么：`i18n` 新增可选的 `sourceLocale`，表示内联元数据文字所用的语言；`defaultLocale` 仍是用户默认语言。`os lint`、`os i18n check`、`os i18n extract` 按它判定源语言；声明了 `sourceLocale` 时，用户默认语言也一并纳入覆盖检查。
- 为什么改：#33232。英文写元数据、默认给用户中文的应用，原来会被误报 446 条"缺 en 翻译"，真正缺的中文反而不报。
- 风险与回滚：放宽（新增可选键）。不声明该键的应用输出逐字节不变。回滚即 revert。
